title: Slowly Changing Dimensions
interviewAnswer: SCD patterns define how dimension changes are represented. Type 1 overwrites history; Type 2 creates dated versions so historical facts can be analyzed with attributes valid at that time.
why: Slowly Changing Dimensions appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: SCD patterns define how dimension changes are represented. Type 1 overwrites history; Type 2 creates dated versions so historical facts can be analyzed with attributes valid at that time. Surrogate keys often support Type 2. Late-arriving changes need policy. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Preserve a customer’s historical segment when the segment changes later.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
